items.title: Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 director thinks devs will eventually "be able to churn out a game in 5 seconds with a prompt," but he hopes they're not any good
items.summary: Guillaume Broche, director of GOTY-sweeping RPG Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, told Konbini's Video Game Club that prompt-generated whole games are coming and 'everyone's a little scared.' Sandfall bars generative AI from creative work — it 'takes away from the joy of creating things' — allowing only case-by-case admin/coding use, after last year's placeholder AI-texture flap.
items.why: The industry's hottest auteur weighing in on text-to-game futures is a fresh, high-cachet voice: he predicts the tech wins but bets against its soul, a crisper stance than the CDPR variant we rejected. Date verified via JSON-LD datePublished.
items.notes: Distinct from the rejected CDPR-doubts cluster (different studio, different speaker, new interview). Sandfall's earlier AI-texture controversy is context, not the story.

items.title: Researchers studying ChatGPT conversations surprised to find one power user churning out thousands of Doki Doki Literature Club pregnancy fics
items.summary: An 'AI Fiction in the Wild' paper presented at Purdue's MFS Cultural AI Conference mined 500k anonymized WildChat ChatGPT logs: over a third involved fiction generation, 2% of users produced 80% of it, and the most-requested game universes were Doki Doki Literature Club, League of Legends, and Freedom Planet — topped by one user generating thousands of DDLC birth fics. PC Gamer contrasts this solipsistic loop with communal human fanfic on AO3.
items.why: A dated, citable study revealing how players actually use LLMs around games — game fandoms dominate AI fan fiction, and consumption is hyper-concentrated. Quirky but data-backed, unlike anything already published in the section.
items.notes: Angle should stay on the study's findings about games fandom + AI, not just the salacious hook. Via IT Media News; primary source is the Purdue conference paper (WildChat dataset, Apr 2023–May 2024 collection).

items.title: Amazon Is Awash With AI-Written Guideslop For Games That Aren't Even Out
items.summary: Kotaku found Amazon flooded with AI-generated 'strategy guides' — hallucinated chapters, AI covers, $20+ price tags — for unreleased games including Alien: Isolation 2, Control: Resonant, and Gears of War: E-Day, from prolific fake authors with dozens of listings. Amazon removed flagged books only for identical ones to reappear immediately.
items.why: Concrete, reported AI-slop-economy story at the intersection of games and publishing platforms: fake guides for games nobody has played yet is a vivid, verifiable scam pattern not covered by any published card.
items.notes: Date verified via Kotaku tag RSS pubDate. Complements (doesn't overlap) the published Steam-side slop stories — this is Amazon's storefront, not Valve's.

items.title: D&D and Magic owner Hasbro is reportedly trying to get child actors from Peppa Pig to sign away their voices to AI
items.summary: An Agents of Young Performers Association open letter signed by 1,000+ performers accuses Hasbro of pressuring Peppa Pig child actors into contracts allowing AI use of their voices across all franchise commercial assets with no extra pay; Hasbro didn't deny being the letter's subject. PC Gamer frames it through Hasbro's game-IP empire (D&D, Magic: The Gathering).
items.why: AI voice-rights precedent from a company that owns some of gaming's biggest IP — the contract language performers sign at Hasbro today shapes AI voice clauses in game credits tomorrow.
items.notes: BORDERLINE for the games section: the underlying story is a children's TV franchise; the games tie is Hasbro-as-game-IP-owner framing (PC Gamer gaming-industry desk). Kotaku ran it 2026-06-25T18:00:22Z (https://kotaku.com/hasbro-force-child-actors-ai-voice-contracts-peppa-pig-2000710552) with no gaming angle.
